search_log: Searched "The Godfather Mario Puzo official excerpt publisher" and related first-chapter queries; Penguin Random House and Google Books offered authorized previews, but the accessible render did not expose sustained prose.
Searched "The Godfather Mario Puzo point of view third person omniscient narrator" and opened explicit whole-book descriptions from Course Hero and LitCharts.
Searched "The Godfather Mario Puzo narrative technique omniscient point of view novel" and opened structural research from Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta and Ca' Foscari University.

Searched for epistolary form, frame narrative, multiple narrators, alternating point of view, and first-person chapters; results discussed shifts among character perspectives but produced no evidence of sustained base narration in another grammatical person.
A public-library-hosted craft text and a Latvian university PDF appeared relevant, but their pages could not be opened reliably, so they were not used as evidence.
person_note: The event quotations repeatedly show a nonparticipating narrator moving among the perceptions, memories, beliefs, and knowledge of multiple characters, including the Don, Michael, Santino, and Mama Corleone. All visible narratorial framing is third person. The many I, we, and you forms occur in dialogue or, in q01560, a locally quoted thought; none establishes a sustained first- or second-person section. Independent structural sources describe the whole novel as third-person omniscient, and targeted searches found no epistolary, framed, or alternating-person structure. The main limitation is that the authorized online samples did not yield accessible sustained prose, but the quote evidence and multiple explicit whole-book sources agree.
